newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand put in a subdued performance on Tuesday as exporter dollar selling offset importer demand and foreigners held largely to the sidelines.
At 1400 GMT, the rand was trading at 4.6530/6580 against the U.S. currency from 4.6540/6570 at Monday's close.
"It's been a pretty controlled market," a trader said.

"We've seen good two-way business with exporters around 4.66 and a few importers around 4.6510. I think we will see it settle down for now although people are targetting 4.68/4.69 by next week, especially if dollar/mark goes higher."
Foreign interest, he added, was minimal.
"London has been there on and off and so has New York...they were a bit long (dollars) and offloaded a bit this morning, but they were taken up by importers who were uncovered."
The dollar posted a near eight-year high in London on Tuesday when it peeked over the 1.88 level against the Deutschmark earlier. In early New York trade it was hovering just under 1.88 at 1.8790/95.
Local traders said the dollar/mark levels to watch would be 1.8850 followed by 1.90 -- levels they said appeared likely to be vaulted within the coming days.
"There is possibility it gets there (to 1.8850) and if it does, we should see the rand at 4.67 to 4.6750," the trader said.
The local currency continued to benefit from the dollar's resurgence, firming to 0.4035/4040 marks from 0.4008/4012 overnight.
It was also last trading at 25.5643/5915 yen from 25.4200/4579 on Monday and at 7.5731/5826 against sterling from 7.5856/5951 previously.
Bonds also moved at a sedentary pace amid a general lack of interest, dealers said.
"It's been a total non-entity of a day," a trader said.
"There was a bit of buying earlier before lunch, a couple of people caught short, but bar that there has been sweet zilch," he added.
At 1400 GMT, the key R150 loan was trading at a 14.145 percent yield from 14.13 percent at Tuesday's finish.
Dealers said the lack of interest in the market appeared to stem from the fact that there was no new news to feed on as well as Thursday's options close-out.
One broker noted that there had been interest in options volatilities, which indicated that if the market did break lower it would move swiftly.
"The volatilties on the options have jumped about 1 percent in the last week which indicates if market breaks down it will move quite fast," he said.
Another trader also noted that there had already been exercising of options by some players which pointed to a relatively smooth close-out on Thursday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners sold a net 38.34 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after selling 295.45 million rand's worth on Friday.
Turnover was 9.65 billion rand compared with Friday's 5.04 billion rand.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage eased to 7.866 billion rand on Saturday from 7.910 billion rand on Friday. Monday's shortage was not immediately available.
Offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.40 to 15.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 14.90 percent.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
